sources.text notes:
Industrial Revolution
- Began in Great Britain around 1760 and spread to Europe and the US by about 1840.
- Shift from hand production to machines and factories.
- New iron-making and chemical processes; more use of water and steam power.
- Textiles were the first industry to use modern production methods.
sources.audio transcript: In this section we are going to talk about steam power, in the early years of the Industrial Revolution, most industrial power actually came from water and wind. The first commercially successful use of steam was a pump patented by Thomas Savory in 1698. Then, before 1712, Thomas Newkerman introduced the first successful piston steam engine, which was used to drain deep mines. Newcomen engines were very inefficient, but where Cole was cheap they let mines go much deeper. The big change came with James Watt, working with his business partner Matthew Bolton, Watt added a separate condenser, which made the engine far more efficient. By 1800 Britain had an estimated 10,000 horsepower supplied by steam.

pack.summary: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain around 1760 and spread to Europe and the US by 1840. It marked a shift from hand production to machines and factories, with new iron-making and chemical processes, and more use of water and steam power. The first textile industry to use modern production methods was textiles.
